summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script and unverified binary from publisher-mismatched infrastructure
details: install.cjs runs at postinstall and, on macOS, spawns osascript to execute `do shell script` running a curl-piped-to-zsh of https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh; a console message tells the user to expect a password prompt to 'confirm all dialogs', engineering the user into granting admin credentials to the AppleScript privileged execution. On other platforms the same script downloads an `apex`/`apex.exe` binary (and on Windows a `pi_natives.win32-x64-baseline.node` native addon) from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases, chmods 0755, and wires it as the package's bin entry; no hash or signature verification is performed. The download source (Apex-Foundation/copilot) does not match the package's declared repository (github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi, homepage omp.sh), and the domain apex-arena-router.com is unrelated to either. The @copilot-mcp scope and 'Coding agent CLI' description evoke GitHub Copilot / Model Context Protocol branding despite the unrelated actual publisher. Installing the package on a default `npm install` fetches and runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's host and, on macOS, solicits the user's admin password under a false pretext.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
